title: Symptom Classifier response
description: The one JSON object the session LLM (DeepSeek V4 Flash) returns per session, at form submit. See ../C1-classifier-response.md for the full spec and reasoning. This schema checks shape and the global S3 tag enum. It doesn't check that a tag or variant is applicable to the specific device_id in the response; that check needs the loaded device catalog and is M12's responsibility.

device_id.description: Echoed back from the device already selected on the Landing screen, in canonical kebab-case, e.g. 'iphone-14'. The model just returns this field it doesn't classify it. M12 hard-rejects a response whose device_id doesn't match the request's -- that's a validation failure, not a low-confidence case.

condition.description: Normalized device condition. Both values exist because the Market Data Service's cache key treats condition as its own axis (PRD S6B.2). The v1 self-diagnosis flow only ever describes a device reported as broken, so this resolves to 'broken' in practice.

variant.description: The device's price-driving spec tier (catalog variant_key_field) in lowercase-kebab form, e.g. '128gb'; 'base' for a device with no variant axis; or null when it can't be resolved. Never a guess -- a wrong value here writes a wrong price into the shared 30-day market cache for every later user of that device/variant. A base device should never emit null.

issues.description: Map of S3 tag id to an independent probability in [0, 1]. Values don't need to sum to 1 -- multiple issues can co-occur, e.g. water damage raising several tags at once. A tag left out is implicitly 0. Keys are restricted to the ten S3 tag ids, so an invented tag fails validation.

confidence.description: Confidence, in [0, 1], that the issues probabilities are complete enough to act on without a follow-up question. Scoped to issues only -- variant uncertainty is signaled separately, via variant: null. The threshold that triggers a follow-up is C6's call, measured against C2's test set.
